known_failed_or_superseded_qa_attempts: An initial synthetic browser harness did not wait for a new document after reload; navigation synchronization was corrected.
A synthetic fixture retained a duplicate fixed draft ID across reruns; catalog validation correctly rejected it, and later fixture runs reset their private state.
Mobile review found history-table screen-reader text overflowing the viewport and a new-run target below44pixels; the actual frontend was corrected and final390/320checks passed.
The first actual browser script had a selector quoting syntax error before page work; the script was corrected and syntax-checked.
A saved-draft assertion matched an older visible draft while the new save was still loading; later checks wait for the exact new run identity.

An otherwise passing actual workflow captured two installed-browser-extension script requests. A clean isolated browser with extensions disabled passed all30 final checks with only local page requests.
An owned-browser cleanup guard rejected Chrome process-title formatting; executable and exact private profile checks were used before restarting only the task-owned browser processes.
limitations: Draft creation and browser verification do not establish a paid run, useful agent concurrency, merged delivery, accepted quality or an AFK advantage.
Historical screenshot data describe their original capture time rather than current provider activity.
The screenshot timestamps are local file-write observations following browser capture, not provider execution timestamps.
Earlier syntax-error console output is retained in the tool transcript; it has no separate original private raw-output file.
